extracted.intended_audience: War Department / Army administrators, military lawyers, and officials advising on personnel, procurement, and cadet matters
extracted.subtask_description: Collection of early-20th-century Army legal opinions and administrative rules covering (inter alia) government representation in litigation, Secretary of War authorities, cadet appointment and discipline rules, enlisted/noncommissioned officer rights, and appropriation usages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government representation in private litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: The United States is not obligated to represent private litigants or provide counsel where the United States is not a party and has no legal interest in the suit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Parents suing a railroad for a soldier's death — since U.S. not a party, no obligation to represent them (C.164-78, June 16, 1904). Contrast with cases where suit grew out of military service or government-authorized activity, which have led to representation or recommendation for counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances warranting government-provided counsel to officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an activity (e.g., a company exchange) existed by the authority of a commanding officer or other peculiar circumstances tied the litigation to official duties, it may be proper for officers sued to request counsel provided by the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: A company exchange carried on at a post with commanding officer's consent — counsel provision advised (C.19268, Mar. 1, 1906; C.20279, Apr. 20, 1907). Consider whether the disputed acts were authorized or directly connected to official duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government will not resist execution of affirmed judgments
rubrics_metrics.description: When litigation against an officer results in a judgment that has been rendered and affirmed by the court of last resort, the Government will not be warranted in furnishing counsel or taking affirmative action to resist execution of that judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Officer sued for alleged undue severity in removing trespassing animals — judgment affirmed; Government not required to resist execution (C.22007, Apr. 13, 1911).

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to DOJ for alleged fraud by former soldiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a discharged volunteer made fraudulent final statements presented to a paymaster, the matter should be referred to the Department of Justice for prosecution under applicable statutes (e.g., section 5438, K. S. C. 7284).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Fraudulent final statements by a discharged volunteer — refer to DOJ (Nov. 1899).

rubrics_metrics.name: Congressional relief favored when officers acted under apparent lawful orders
rubrics_metrics.description: If officers performed acts in good faith and in discharge of what they believed to be public duty under departmental orders, and were later adjudged liable (even by the Supreme Court), an application to Congress for appropriation to defray the judgment may properly be favored by the Secretary of War.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 1873 judgment subsequently affirmed in 1877 — despite illegality determination, Secretary of War could favor relief (R.41,433, Oct. 1878). Consider whether action was in good faith under orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relief for disbursing officer on short consignment
rubrics_metrics.description: When a disbursing officer's consignment of public money arrived short through no fault of the officer, a proper case for congressional relief may arise and should be recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Recommended relief where shortage not due to officer's fault (C.25605, Feb. 4, 1910).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clothing appropriations include general prisoners
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpretation of Army appropriation acts and regulations: the term 'Army' as used in appropriation relating to clothing includes general prisoners; commanding officers may order necessary issues of clothing (from damaged/unissued supplies) to prisoners who have no clothing allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Secretary of War may authorize overcoats, overshoes, mittens, flannel shirts to general prisoners as charge against clothing appropriation (C.2057, Mar. 1896). See Army Regulations and Circulars for authority to prevent suffering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to order attendants for invalid discharged soldiers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of War may, in exercise of general power over movements of Army members, order a hospital attendant (an enlisted man) to accompany an invalid discharged soldier to the Soldiers' Home.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Held authority to order attendant to accompany invalid discharged soldier (C.2592, Sept. 1896).

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary of War's authority over dredging and navigation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of War has authority to authorize dredging operations insofar as they concern navigation interests but lacks jurisdiction to permit dredging for gold or mining in navigable U.S. waters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple opinions cited (G.7487, Jan. 6, 1900; others 1900–1910). Distinguish navigation-related dredging from mineral-extraction activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility for construction of fortifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of War, not the Secretary of the Navy, is responsible for construction of fortifications and seacoast defenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited holding: O.12389, Apr. 9, 1902. Use this allocation when assigning construction responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits of comity in providing state officials assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: While comity generally suggests facilitating state officials' legal operations, the United States is not obliged to provide facilities that would materially interfere with or embarrass the due prosecution of a public function under an act of Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Secretary of War may decline to order a commanding officer to furnish list of employees for state tax collection (C.1300, Apr. 27, 1895). Balance federal functions vs. state requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using enlisted men as servants
rubrics_metrics.description: Under wording of section 1232, R.S., 'no officer shall use an enlisted man as a servant in any case whatever'; there is no authority to except furloughed soldiers from the statute's operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holding: furloughed soldiers may not lawfully be used as servants by officers (C.1867, Nov. 23, 1895).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of military pay from civil process
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer or soldier cannot be deprived of pay by means of civil attachment or levy on execution; civil judgments (e.g., interlocutory allowance pendente lite) are not to be satisfied out of military pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: cases cited where interlocutory judgment against officer in divorce could not be satisfied from pay (R.8,493, May 1864; C.13097, Aug. 8, 1902).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on officers accepting foreign remuneration or service
rubrics_metrics.description: Absent express congressional authority, an Army officer cannot accept remuneration from a foreign power for military or public services, nor may he be properly granted leave to render foreign service (even without compensation), consistent with Art. I, sec. 9, par. 8 of the Constitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites R.37,148, Apr. 1876; C.20396, Apr. 15, 1910. Consider constitutional prohibition and spirit of laws requiring service to the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gifts from enlisted men incompatible with officer-enlisted relation
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptance by an officer of a present from enlisted men recently under his command is incompatible with proper officer/enlisted relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holding: acceptance of gifts from recent subordinates is improper (C.10102, Mar. 29, 1901).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cadet appointments: President's power and residence requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The power of appointing cadets is in the President; except for at-large appointments, appointments must be made from 'actual residents' of the congressional/territorial district indicated. Members of Congress' nominative privilege is limited to nominating persons who meet statutory requirements; the President must appoint only persons complying with the statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited R.42,601, Apr. 1880; C.6615, June 1899; others. Verify residence qualifications and ensure nominations comply with sections cited (e.g., sec. 1315).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of redistricting on cadet appointees
rubrics_metrics.description: When a State has been redistricted, cadets appointed from former districts should be credited to the new districts that now include their place of residence; conditional appointments made prior to redistricting remain valid; future appointments should follow newly established districts and numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R.39,575, June 1878. Anticipate administrative delay in filling vacancies due to new districting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residence qualification depends on date of appointment
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1317 R.S. prescribes appointment one year in advance; the qualification as to residence (sec. 1315) refers to date of appointment, not date of admission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C.3886, Feb. 1898. Ensure residence is fixed as of the appointment date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domicil of emancipated minor requires animus manendi
rubrics_metrics.description: An emancipated minor's domicil is determined like any other person's: there must be an animus manendi. A temporary residence adopted solely to secure a cadet appointment is not effective to change domicil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R.56,473, Aug. 1888. Scrutinize claimed residences intended solely to qualify for appointment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unemancipated minor's residence tied to parent
rubrics_metrics.description: An unemancipated minor cannot acquire a residence distinct from that of his father or parent for purposes of cadet eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations: R.29,83 (July 1869); others. Emancipation status critical to eligibility analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Officer's temporary duty in a Territory does not confer residency for son's appointment
rubrics_metrics.description: An officer being on duty under military orders in a Territory does not make his minor son eligible for appointment as a cadet from that Territory; the father's temporary duty is insufficient to establish legal residence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R.30,528, July 1870; C.1220, Apr. 1895. Evaluate permanence and legal residence, not mere presence on duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign domicil parent disqualifies minor for district appointment
rubrics_metrics.description: A minor whose father is a foreigner domiciled outside the U.S. and who is in the U.S. only for education is not eligible for a cadet appointment from a congressional district.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R.35,446, June 1874. Verify parents' domicil when assessing eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional/'alternate' cadet appointments not recognized by statute
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional appointments made as alternates by Members of Congress are not recognized in statute; a provisional appointee has only the original claim to present himself for examination, and is not entitled to be substituted automatically when a regular nominee resigns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R.44,162, Feb. 1879. Avoid treating provisional nominees as having statutory entitlement to fill vacancies created by resignation of the regular appointee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alaska is an organized Territory for cadet appointment purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Alaska is an organized Territory within the meaning of sec. 1315, R.S., and a cadet may lawfully be appointed from that Territory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C.19179, Feb. 10, 1906. Use when clarifying territorial appointment eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cadet age admission limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1318, R.S., prescribes admission of appointees only between ages 17 and 22; an appointee not 17 until the preceding August may take the June exam and, if qualified, remain at the academy at own expense until of lawful age to be admitted. A cadet over 22 separated from the Academy is not eligible for reappointment or reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C.3886, Feb. 1898; C.3852, Feb. 8, 1898. Check age as of statutory dates and academy year start (Sept. 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Divorce status and cadet eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who has obtained a divorce a vinculo matrimonii is prima facie an unmarried man under Academy Regulations and is eligible for appointment upon presentation of an authenticated copy of the absolute divorce decree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C.27225, Sept. 7, 1910. Require authenticated state decree for proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: President's power to reappoint same nominee to his own vacancy
rubrics_metrics.description: The President is empowered under sec. 1317, R.S., to reappoint a regular appointee who resigned to fill his own vacancy when that vacancy has not been filled in the meantime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R.37,195, Feb. 1871. Distinguish from situations where vacancy has been filled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reappointment restrictions for cadets deficient in conduct or studies
rubrics_metrics.description: By sec. 1325, R.S., the President would not be empowered to reappoint a cadet discharged as deficient in conduct or studies except upon recommendation of the academic board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R.44,372, July 1880; C.3796, Jan. 1898; C.16602, July 1904. Academic board recommendation is prerequisite to reappointment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on reappointment after dismissal by general court-martial
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1325's prohibition on reappointment for cadets found deficient in conduct applies to cadets dismissed by sentence of general court-martial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: a.29329, Dec. 26, 1911. Treat court-martial dismissals as grounds barring reappointment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary of War may grant furlough without pay to cadet recommended for discharge
rubrics_metrics.description: A cadet found deficient and recommended for discharge was lawfully granted furlough without pay by the Secretary of War; such an exercise of authority is legitimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C.15709, Jan. 16, 1901. Use furlough as administrative tool pending discharge process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary's duty to execute academic board recommendations is ministerial
rubrics_metrics.description: In view of sec. 1325, the Secretary of War's duty in executing the findings and recommendation of the academic board regarding deficient cadets is ministerial in character; cadets reported deficient should not be reappointed absent board recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C.3796, July 23, 1884. Administrative officers should follow board findings rather than exercise independent discretion to reappoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cadet amenability to court-martial
rubrics_metrics.description: Cadets are amenable to trial by court-martial for violations of academy regulations constituting 'conduct to the prejudice of good order and military discipline.' Records of trials by general courts-martial appointed by the superintendent go to the Secretary of War for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R.36,129 (Dec. 1874); C.15821, Jan. 20, 1904. Distinguish military offenses from mere school discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on superintendent's disciplinary jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: The superintendent of the Military Academy cannot, by academy regulation, try and punish a cadet for a military offense for which under the Articles of War the cadet is amenable to trial by court-martial; regulations conferring such power would be in contravention of law and inoperative. Reductions under regulations may be regarded as school discipline and do not bar separate court-martial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: P.61,373 (Sept. 1893); C.9704, Jan. 6, 1910. President may suspend a cadet without pay under regulations (C.10513, May 20, 1901).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative dismissal for hazing vs. criminal prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: The act of March 2, 1901 is construed to allow administrative dismissal by the Secretary of War for hazing on superintendent investigation assisted by boards; however, where the act charged involves criminality beyond hazing, trial by court-martial may be resorted to and is preferable. Procedure for hazing later regulated by April 19, 1910 act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C.9704, Jan. 6, 1910; C.29329, Dec. 27, 1911. Assess whether conduct is purely administrative hazing or rises to crime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for cadet name changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of War will not change a cadet's name on the Academy register simply on application; the cadet should procure the name change under his State's statutes and then the register may be amended to correspond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: P.25,126 (June 1888). Follow civil statutory procedures for legal name changes before altering administrative registers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mileage entitlement for cadets performing special duty
rubrics_metrics.description: Cadets ordered from West Point to Washington for special duty and returning are not entitled to mileage since they are not commissioned officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C.24762, Apr. 12, 1909. Distinguish commissioned status when computing travel allowances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graduation leave rules and non-cumulativeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Act of Dec. 20, 1886 grants leaves of absence to graduates from date of graduation; leave with pay from date of graduation (approx. June 12) to Sept. 30 is warranted; such leaves are not cumulative. Time ordered back to duty during graduating leave should be deducted from leave and may be used after Sept. 30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C.13346, Dec. 8, 1903; C.13346, Apr. 17, 1908. Adjust service records for duty performed during leave.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warrant/certificate of noncommissioned officer is personal property
rubrics_metrics.description: The warrant or certificate given to a noncommissioned officer is as much the personal property of the individual as a commission is to a commissioned officer; absent statute/regulation requiring surrender on reduction or dishonorable discharge, he may retain it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R.40,310 (July 1878). Check statutes/regulations for surrender requirements before demanding return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection from reduction while absent due to wounds/disability
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph 271 forbids reduction of a noncommissioned officer while absent on account of wounds or disability incurred in line of duty; paragraph 268 vests selection of certain sergeants in company commanders — read together, relief from detail to another NCO of same grade is not a 'reduction' within paragraph 271. However, reduction for inefficiency or incapacity, even if effected while absent due to sickness, is not within the paragraph's prohibition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C.25760 (Nov. 6, 1909; Oct. 4, 1910; Jan. 20, 1911). Apply nuance: medical absence due to duty-provided wounds gives protection; inefficiency-based reduction does not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissary sergeant appointment service requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1142 R.S. authorizes appointment of commissary sergeants from 'sergeants of the line' who have faithfully served five years, three of which must be in grade as noncommissioned officers; service as a commissioned officer (e.g., U.S. Volunteers) cannot be computed as time served in the grade of noncommissioned officer required by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C.6793, Aug. 1899. Count only qualifying NCO service toward statutory requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post quartermaster sergeant selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the act of July 5, 1884, post quartermaster sergeants shall be selected by examination from the most competent enlisted men who have served at least four years and whose character and education fit them to take charge of public property and act as clerks/assistants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: P.A.7,169, May 1891. Secretary of War may appoint any enlisted man found to possess the specified qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority required prior to placing enlisted men on extra duty
rubrics_metrics.description: Army Regulations requiring that enlisted men of staff departments not be placed on extra duty without War Department authority contemplate that such authority be obtained prior to detaching the soldier; this allows the Secretary to pass on the case and avoid hardship and the need for nunc pro tunc action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C.17173, Nov. 17, 1904. Seek prior approval to prevent retroactive corrections and unfairness to the soldier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlisted men and civil office: statutory silence but practical incompatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Although section 1222 R.S. does not in terms apply to enlisted men (and law does not expressly forbid an enlisted man serving as postmaster), in general it is incompatible with an enlisted man's status and obligations to hold civil office; by analogy enlisted men should be prevented from holding or exercising civil office in most cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C.15297, Nov. 27, 1909; R.37,616, June 1877. Consider rare exceptions (e.g., ordnance sergeant at permanent station) but be cautious about permanent civil employment or foreign government detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlisted detail to assist ordnance mechanic falls within enlistment duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailing enlisted men to assist an ordnance mechanic in altering concrete emplacements for seacoast artillery is duty which a soldier is expected to perform under his enlistment contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C.14591, May 4, 1905. Use enlistment scope to evaluate assignment legitimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chief musician status as enlisted specialist
rubrics_metrics.description: A chief musician is an enlisted man (not a noncommissioned officer) enlisted to perform as an instructor of music; he cannot legally be reduced to the ranks, may be tried by regimental or garrison court as well as general court, and may pursue his profession in civil life after term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R.33,33 May 1872; C.24179, Dec. 7, 1908. Treat musical instructors as a distinct category with special protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to obey civil subpoenas and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: An enlisted man personally served with a civil subpoena to attend as a witness before a civil court (where his post is not under exclusive U.S. jurisdiction) who neglects to comply may be guilty of contempt and, if fined by the court, has no remedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: P.35,284 Sept. 1889. Distinguish jurisdictional settings; personal service matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'Regular Army' vs 'Volunteer Army'
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'Regular Army' refers to the standing Army the Government ordinarily maintains indefinitely (peace or war) and is composed of persons who engage voluntarily and directly with the United States to serve; it is not defined by the method of bringing forces into service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C.1301, Mar. 1895; C.21406, Apr. 19, 1907. Use when distinguishing force types and their intended permanence/character.
